comparator.name: Business Administration
comparator.sourceNotes: The exact target is the Dutch-taught full-time BSc Bedrijfskunde, CROHO50645, distinct from English IBA. Appendix3 of the2026–2027 OER pp33–34 lists ten6ECfirst-year components, ten6ECsecond-year components, three6ECadvanced third-year courses,30ECfree choice and12ECthesis:25components totalling180EC. The renewed degree starts from2024–2025; current B2/B3 page cohorts are compatible, not an inter-cohort credit mixture. However the formal thesis-entry conflict means this numerical180EC structure cannot be certified as a formally valid complete pathway. Other applicable rules are verified independently. September49-page edition supersedes the older July47-page edition for citation; both visibly repeat the thesis conflict.
components: Introduction to Behaviour in Organisations and Work

30 EC of free choice in third-year semester 1. University courses, an 18-EC minor plus further courses, study abroad or an internship require approval and non-overlap. OER Article 17 permits 6, 12 or 24-EC internships; no internship or minor is compulsory.

Clarify the controlling 2026–2027 thesis-entry requirement for the Dutch Bedrijfskunde programme MAN-BPRO372A. The latest September OER Appendix 4 p35 requires at least102 EC including Academic Skills and Onderzoeks- en Interventiemethodologie A and B, which are absent under those names from the renewed Appendix3 curriculum. The current official2026 Osiris course172589 instead requires102 EC including BIN117B, BPRA171 and BPRO100A. An authoritative amendment, explicit equivalence/transition rule or precedence statement is needed to reconcile these current official conditions. No exemption, replacement equivalence or administrative error is assumed.

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI

core: Organisations, organisational processes, design and change
Strategy, marketing, human resources, leadership and value creation
Responsible and sustainable entrepreneurship, ethics and wider social impact
Accounting, finance, economics and operations for organisational decisions
Quantitative, qualitative and independent empirical research into organisations
Technology, digitalisation, innovation and data-informed organisational change
questions: How can organisations survive continuous change and improve their processes?
How can data, digital technology and innovation improve organisational decisions?
How can organisations create economic, social and environmental value responsibly?

trace: Direct accounting contribution: accepted accounting theory and practice, corporate annual reports and financial-statement analysis support organisational decisions. The title alone does not establish the whole external corporate-finance syllabus.
examines managerial, organisational and societal implications of AI and technological change
covers legal frameworks for contracts, trade, company activity and digital commerce across borders

Direct financial decision-making: cases develop analysis of financial data, risk, investment, budgeting and business value. This is partial corporate-finance correspondence, not identical external coverage.
provides economic foundations on firms, markets, incentives and macroeconomic conditions
examines growth, inflation, business cycles and policy shaping the international business environment
develops microeconomic and behavioural analysis of consumer and firm decisions
examines market failure, externalities, taxation and public intervention affecting firms
provides econometric tools for causal and predictive analysis of business data
develops product innovation through customer needs, design, costing and team development
examines marketing strategy, consumer psychology and responsible customer engagement
develops business strategy from vision to execution and responsible digital transformation

Direct applied empirical business research: students plan and conduct real market research, analyse results and formulate business recommendations. This course-based project does not reproduce a separate 12-EC bachelor thesis.
examines institutions, culture, governance and corporate responsibility in global business
provides business foundations while developing venture creation, business models and market validation
provides research design, surveys, experiments and statistical analysis for management questions
develops leadership theory, self-awareness and applied leadership practice
develops leadership communication, ethical influence and persuasive practice
examines inclusive leadership and diversity management in organisations
examines motivation, groups, organisational culture and structures through organisational psychology
Direct business negotiation and influence: persuasive arguments, language, negotiation processes and interest-based strategic interaction. This is not a general corporate-strategy counterpart.
examines ethical and societal questions raised by artificial intelligence
Complementary analytical tools: provides relational database and SQL skills for structured data. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

Complementary analytical tools: develops algorithmic problem-solving and data structures for computational applications. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

Complementary analytical tools: develops data cleaning, visualisation and manipulation across disciplinary datasets. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.
introduces machine-learning models for prediction and analysis of real datasets
Complementary analytical tools: develops neural-network and deep-learning methods for advanced AI applications. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.
Complementary analytical tools: provides programming foundations in Python. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.
Complementary analytical tools: provides mathematical foundations for quantitative modelling. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.
Complementary analytical tools: provides linear-algebra foundations for quantitative and machine-learning models. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

Complementary analytical tools: provides probability, statistical inference and simulation foundations for risk and analytics. Application to business is supplied by the programme, not guaranteed in this course.

Complementary regulatory and societal context: governmental and nongovernmental actors, interests, public opinion and policy enforcement explain sustainability governance. This is not a dedicated responsible-organisation course.
Complementary environmental framework: planetary boundaries identify environmental limits relevant to responsible products and business strategy; this is not business management training.
Complementary climate context: anthropogenic drivers, environmental and societal impacts, adaptation, mitigation, climate governance and justice inform sustainable business risk and responsibility.
Direct sustainable product and process analysis: life-cycle environmental evaluation and strategic circular-economy planning support responsible enterprise decisions.

Complementary normative reasoning: virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism, responsibility, equality, wealth, future generations and climate support ethical business judgments. No dedicated business-ethics case syllabus is claimed.

Complementary empirical method: qualitative question design, interpretation, small-team projects and reflexivity about complexity and power support organisational inquiry; business topics are not guaranteed.

Complementary behavioural foundations: scientific social psychology examines how others influence thought, feelings and behaviour; its organisational or customer application is specific supporting work.

Complementary academic and professional communication: rhetorical analysis, argument, academic writing and oral presentation support communicating organisational research. Historical and contemporary rhetoric is not an empirical business-research course.

alternatives.label: Business administration, organisations & strategy
alternatives.concept: A broad closest feasible Business Administration programme combining organisations and change, strategy, marketing, entrepreneurship, leadership and people management with accounting, finance, economics, qualitative and quantitative research, data, technology and international governance.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum integrates organisational behaviour and leadership with strategy, marketing, entrepreneurship, accounting, finance, economics, research, technology and international governance.
progression: Business, economics, data, quantitative and qualitative methods, leadership and communication support later marketing, organisational psychology, econometrics, market research and international governance. The early Strategy course has no formal prerequisite. All assigned offerings and formal prerequisites pass; advisory progression does not create extra hard constraints.

alternatives.label: Business analytics & digital transformation
alternatives.concept: A related business-analytics direction combining a sustained business core in entrepreneurship, strategy, accounting, economics, marketing, organisational psychology, international governance and empirical market research with programming, databases, mathematics, machine learning and responsible AI. Technical courses provide analytical tools; dedicated organisation design, systems theory and the full business-function sequence remain gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum combines business strategy, organisations, marketing and economics with programming, databases, mathematics, statistics, machine learning, deep learning, algorithms and responsible AI.
alternatives.distinctness: Ten courses differ from the broad programme. Specific computational and mathematical methods replace part of its leadership, finance and qualitative-methods sequence. The retained business core makes this a related analytics direction, not an equivalent general Business Administration qualification.
progression: Business, programming, data, research and mathematical foundations precede advanced strategy, algorithms, machine learning, deep learning, international business and market research. Mathematical Methods precedes linear algebra, probability and deep learning; programming precedes algorithms. All formal prerequisites occur earlier and every course is offered in its assigned term.

alternatives.label: Responsible entrepreneurship & sustainable strategy
alternatives.concept: A business programme centred on responsible entrepreneurship and sustainable strategy: venture creation, accounting, finance, economics, marketing, organisational psychology, business law, international governance and empirical research. Life-cycle analysis directly supports sustainable products and processes; climate, planetary boundaries, ethics and public sustainability governance provide specific complementary contexts.
alternatives.labelReason: Business functions and research carry the main curricular weight. Four environmental science and technology courses are replaced by qualitative methods, data analysis, AI governance and finance; sustainability is applied to business decisions rather than asserted from environmental coherence alone.
alternatives.distinctness: The emphasis is responsible business and sustainable products, supported by environmental limits, climate, life-cycle assessment, ethics and policy context. Pairwise course differences are [6, 12]. Four weak science/technology placements are replaced by business, finance and empirical methods; the organising academic direction remains distinct.
progression: Business and research foundations precede advanced business law, finance, international governance, organisational psychology and empirical market research. Planetary boundaries precedes life-cycle analysis and sustainability governance. Every formal prerequisite and assigned offering is checked directly against the current workbook.

routeSelection.basis: The exact target names the Dutch-taught Bedrijfskunde specialisation. The current programme factsheet and OER distinguish it from English-taught International Business Administration. No optional minor is selected as a compulsory route or for UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Three provisional, evidence-backed concepts remain: broad business administration; business analytics and digital transformation; responsible entrepreneurship and sustainable strategy. Each contains sustained actual business study; a coherent adjacent STEM degree would not suffice under the CP119 distinction. Four environmental science/technology placements in the third route are replaced with directly useful business and research content. Pairwise differences are [{'pair': [1, 2], 'differentCourses': 10}, {'pair': [1, 3], 'differentCourses': 6}, {'pair': [2, 3], 'differentCourses': 12}]. Three is the maximum, not a target. Final comparative approval is withheld because current official thesis-entry sources conflict.

blocks: Partial production correspondence: consumer-product development includes customer needs, fabrication method, costs and sustainability. It does not reproduce a full operations-management and logistics course.
Partial business-strategy correspondence: strategic planning from vision to execution and responsible digital transformation. The external strategy sequence is broader.
Both develop entrepreneurship through venture design, market validation and business planning; UCR explicitly includes social entrepreneurship.
UCR offers strategy and strategic-thinking courses but no separate advanced strategy course in the selected curricula.
A dedicated integrated introduction to marketing and strategy. UCR supplies these subjects across separate business courses, without assigning one course twice.
Partial people-management correspondence: diversity, inclusion and ethical collaborative leadership. This is not the full strategic human-resource management function.
Both examine behaviour, motivation and leadership within organisations; UCR uses organisational psychology as its frame.
UCR studies organisations and leadership across several courses but has no single dedicated organisation-theory counterpart.
UCR covers organisational behaviour, strategy and leadership but has no dedicated organisation-design course.
UCR addresses organisational change across strategy, leadership and digital-transformation courses, but no single dedicated course reproduces this component.
UCR has no dedicated organisational systems-theory course in the current enriched catalogue.
Both develop accounting knowledge and the use of financial reporting for organisational decisions.
Partial finance correspondence through financial-data analysis, risk, investment and budgeting; no identical corporate-finance syllabus is claimed.
Both introduce economic reasoning about firms, markets and the wider economy.
Both provide advanced quantitative analysis for organisational questions; UCR focuses on econometric estimation and inference.
Both examine marketing strategy, consumer behaviour and responsible customer engagement.

Partial empirical-research correspondence: a real market-research project, analysis and recommendations. The UCR course is 7.5 EC and course-based; it is not the separate required 12-EC bachelor thesis, whose formal entry rule is unresolved.
Both introduce research design, statistics and quantitative analysis.
Both develop qualitative research design, data collection, interpretation and methodological reflexivity.
UCR combines data, research and responsible-management courses, but no single scheduled course reproduces this integrated business-analysis component.
Both analyse how digital technologies and AI reshape organisations, innovation and managerial decisions.
Dedicated study of responsible organisation. Sustainability governance supplies public-policy context and does not reproduce this organisational unit.
Both develop academic source use, argument, communication, collaboration and reflective professional skills.
Partial ethical-method correspondence: normative theories, responsibility and applied moral argument. UCR does not promise the dedicated business-ethics syllabus.
This is genuine free-choice space. UCR flexibility is distributed across the complete 180-EC curriculum, so no single scheduled course is asserted as its equivalent.

notes.text: UCR offers substantive business, analytical and responsible-enterprise study, with gaps in dedicated organisation theory/design, systems theory, operations/logistics and a separate12ECthesis. The external degree cannot yet be certified because two current official sources give different thesis-entry prerequisites.

audience.programmeDescription: The Dutch-taught Bedrijfskunde degree studies how organisations function and change. It combines strategy, marketing, people, finance, economics, responsible enterprise and empirical organisational research.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The published credit structure is shown while conflicting official thesis-entry requirements are clarified. A complete UCR comparison is withheld; this does not mean that UCR has no relevant business programme.

curriculum.limitation: The 25 published components sum to 180 EC, but current official thesis-entry requirements conflict. This table shows the supported credit structure; it is not a certified complete degree pathway. UCR comparisons remain withheld pending authoritative clarification.

componentNotes.ba3-free: 30 EC of free choice in third-year semester 1. University courses, an 18-EC minor plus further courses, study abroad or an internship require approval and non-overlap. OER Article 17 permits 6, 12 or 24-EC internships; no internship or minor is compulsory.
componentNotes.ba3-thesis: The OER and current official course catalogue both require at least 102 EC, but name different prerequisite courses. Their controlling relationship needs authoritative clarification before this degree pathway can be certified.
componentNotes.ba1-skills: The academic Dutch-language test is a mandatory first-year requirement linked to a course; it does not add credits. Current full-time first-year study advice normally requires 42 of 60 EC, with personal circumstances considered.
